claim: 7 state-of-the-art open-source multi-agent LLM systems fail 41% to 86.7% of the time on their respective benchmarks, based on empirical analysis of 1,642 annotated execution traces.
stance_target: multi-agent systems in production are unreliable at a scale that demands robust self-monitoring and lifecycle management, including termination logic
scope_conditions: 7 MAS frameworks (ChatDev, MetaGPT, HyperAgent, AppWorld, AG2, Magentic-One, OpenManus) across coding, math, general-agent tasks
quoted_support: Our empirical analysis reveals 41% to 86.7% failure rate on 7 state-of-the-art (SOTA) open-source MAS detailed in Figure 5 (Appendix B).

claim: The MAST taxonomy defines Failure Mode 1.5 'Unaware of termination conditions' as a system-design failure: lack of recognition of criteria that should trigger interaction termination, leading to unnecessary continuation -- an empirically observed and named failure pattern directly describing agents that fail to self-terminate when they should.
stance_target: agents in production genuinely fail to self-terminate correctly, validating the need for explicit auto-kill/idle-detection mechanisms rather than relying on model judgment alone
quoted_support: FM-1.5: Unaware of termination conditions - Lack of recognition or understanding of the criteria that should trigger the termination of the agents' interaction, potentially leading to unnecessary continuation.

claim: The MAST taxonomy defines Failure Mode 3.1 'Premature termination' as ending a dialogue, interaction, or task before all necessary information has been exchanged or objectives have been met, resulting in incomplete or incorrect outcomes -- this is a top-level 'Task Verification' failure category (31.41% of category-level failures in the 150-trace human-annotated set).
stance_target: aggressive auto-kill of idle/seemingly-done agents is risk-free; empirically, premature termination is itself a major documented failure mode
scope_conditions: Multi-Agent System Failure Taxonomy (MAST), 150-trace human-annotated subset
quoted_support: FM-3.1: Premature termination - Ending a dialogue, interaction or task before all necessary information has been exchanged or objectives have been met, potentially resulting in incomplete or incorrect outcomes.

claim: A case study on ChatDev found the CPO agent exhibited FM-1.2 (Disobey Role Specification) by terminating a conversation without the CEO agent's consensus; redesigning the workflow so the CEO agent held final termination authority increased overall task success rate by +9.4 percentage points.
stance_target: centralizing termination authority in a single designated agent/role is a concrete, empirically validated design pattern for safe auto-termination in multi-agent systems
scope_conditions: ChatDev multi-agent software-development framework, case study in MAST paper Appendix H
quoted_support: the CPO agent in ChatDev can exhibit 'Failure Mode 1.2 - Disobey Role Specification' by terminating conversation without the CEO agent's consensus. We demonstrate that a straightforward system workflow adjustment ensuring the CEO had the final say contributed to a +9.4% increase in overall task success rate.

claim: MAST's 14 failure modes cluster into three categories by prevalence in the 150-trace human-annotated dataset: System Design Issues (37.17%), Inter-Agent Misalignment (31.41%), and Task Verification (31.41%) -- with 'Unaware of Termination Conditions' and 'Information Withholding' noted as failure types spanning multiple conversation stages (pre-execution, execution, post-execution).
stance_target: taxonomy and prevalence breakdown of why multi-agent systems fail, useful baseline for designing monitoring/self-termination logic
scope_conditions: MAST-Data, 150-trace human-annotated subset, five MAS frameworks
quoted_support: Certain failures, such as 1.5 Unaware of Termination Conditions and 2.4 [Information Withholding span multiple conversation stages]

claim: The MAST authors built an LLM-as-a-Judge annotation pipeline (based on OpenAI's o1 model) achieving kappa=0.77 agreement with human expert annotators on in-distribution data and kappa=0.79 on two additional unseen MAS/benchmarks, released as a pip-installable library (agentdash) for scalable failure-mode monitoring.
stance_target: automated, scalable failure-mode detection (including termination-related failures) in production agent fleets is already demonstrated as technically feasible
scope_conditions: MAST LLM annotator validated on MAST-Data and two additional unseen MAS/benchmarks
quoted_support: We calibrate the LLM annotator to achieve high agreement with human expert annotations (kappa = 0.77), and additionally validated applicability on two additional unseen MAS and benchmarks (kappa = 0.79).
